question: About how many standard chest X-rays deliver the same radiation dose as one CT scan of the abdomen?
move: Put two risks in the same unit before calling them similar.
trap: Guessing a handful, picturing both as one quick picture.
hint: Put both doses in millisieverts, the unit of radiation dose, then divide.
steps: A single chest X-ray taken from behind: about 0.02 mSv.
A CT scan of the abdomen: about 8 mSv.

diagram.caption: One abdominal CT gives the dose of 400 chest X-rays.

reference: Mettler, Huda, Yoshizumi & Mahesh, Effective doses in radiology and diagnostic nuclear medicine: a catalog, Radiology, 2008
